heroHeadline: Von der Leyen Proposes Canada Associate Membership, European Security Council in 2026 State of the Union
heroSubtitle: On September 16, Commission President Ursula von der Leyen used her annual State of the Union address in Strasbourg to propose Canada as the EU's first 'associate member' and back a new European Security Council coordinating the EU, UK, Norway, Ukraine and Canada against hybrid threats, alongside a European Heatwave Plan, a Ceuta-inspired migration emergency framework, and an EU Kids Act restricting under-15 social media features. The speech followed the European Parliament's September 15 adoption of the European Democracy Shield report (420-220-26), which names Russia as the EU's principal hybrid-warfare threat and proposes an EU Centre for Democratic Resilience. On the economic front, the ECB raised its deposit rate to 2.50% on September 10 after August HICP inflation hit 3.3%, a three-year high driven by Middle East conflict-linked energy costs; the EU-US trade deal's implementing legislation still awaits ratification by all 27 member states.
